title: PlayStation Plus November Games Add Dead Island 2 and Tomb Raider Remasters
excerpt: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Monster Train 2 are claimable by all PS Plus members from November 3 to November 30, with October's games leaving on November 2.
body:
• Sony's PlayStation Plus monthly games for November 2026 are Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Monster Train 2, available to all PS Plus tiers including Essential.
  • Members can claim all three from Tuesday, November 3 until Monday, November 30; claimed games stay playable while the membership remains active.
  • Dead Island 2 and Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered run on PS5 and PS4; Monster Train 2 is PS5 only.
  • October's games — F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896 and Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 — leave the lineup on Monday, November 2, so claim them before then if you want them.

Sony announced the PlayStation Plus monthly games for November 2026 on Wednesday: Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Monster Train 2. All three will be available to PlayStation Plus members — including the entry-level Essential tier — from Tuesday, November 3 to Monday, November 30, according to the PlayStation Blog.

Members need to add the games to their library during that window. Once claimed, the games remain playable for as long as the subscription stays active, Push Square noted, even after the next lineup rotates in on December 1.

Dead Island 2 headlines the month

Dead Island 2 is the month's lead title, for PS5 and PS4. The first-person action RPG is set in a zombie-overrun Los Angeles — "HELL-A" in the game's wording — where players work through quests, meet survivors and fight through the city with melee weapons. It can be played alone or in online co-op for up to three players, Sony said.

https://x.com/screenrant/status/2115498867479175562

Push Square, which reviewed the PS5 version at 7 out of 10, described it as a fun and simple zombie-slasher experience, praising its setting, brutal melee combat and graphics while criticizing its RPG elements and loot cycle. For subscribers who skipped the game at its 2023 release, November is a low-cost way in: claiming it in the window costs nothing beyond the existing membership.

Three Lara Croft games in one collection

Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered, also for PS5 and PS4, collects the Darkness Trilogy: Tomb Raider: The Last Revelation, Tomb Raider: Chronicles and Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness. Players can switch between the original polygonal models and the remastered graphics at any time during play, Sony said.

Push Square rated the collection 7 out of 10 on PS5, concluding that a generous selection of modern options balances out the imperfections of The Last Revelation and Chronicles, and that having The Angel of Darkness in a playable state might be worth the price alone. Subscribers who claimed the earlier Tomb Raider I-III Remastered collection through PS Plus can now hold the original six-game run in one library.

Monster Train 2 is the PS5-only pick

Monster Train 2 is a single-player deckbuilding roguelite for PS5 only. Players command clans formed from an alliance of angels and demons against the Titans, who have seized control of Heaven, defending three vertical levels aboard a train through Hell, Heaven and the Abyss. The game offers five new clans, each with its own strengths, and asks players to recruit units and upgrade cards to build a working strategy, according to Sony.

Push Square pointed to a Metacritic rating of 87 for the PC version. PS4 owners cannot play this one, though they can still add it to their library through the PlayStation app or web store during the claim window and download it later if they move to a PS5.

Claim October's games before November 2

The practical deadline arrives before November's games do. PlayStation Plus members have until Monday, November 2 to add October's monthly games — F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896 and Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 — to their libraries, Sony reminded subscribers. After that date those three leave the monthly lineup.

For diaspora households where a single console is shared across generations of players, November's mix is unusually broad: a co-op zombie game older players can play together online, a nostalgia collection for anyone who played Lara Croft on the original PlayStation, and a strategy card game for solo play. The only action required is remembering the two dates — November 2 for October's games, November 30 for November's.
